title: API 653 Tank Shell Wall-Loss Evaluation from C-Scan and Histogram Exports (TK-731, Coveñas)
goal: Perform an in-service API 653 wall loss evaluation on a crude oil storage tank shell plate using C-scan ultrasonic mapping and thickness histogram analysis, assess fluid-induced internal corrosion risks, and draft an API 653 compliance report.
context: Perform an NDT fitness-for-service evaluation of a crude oil storage tank shell plate in Colombia using Ultrasonic C-Scan B-scan data and thickness histograms, applying API 653 code standards to determine structural compliance and corrosion mechanisms.
occupation: Metallurgical Engineer & Senior NDT / QA/QC Welding Inspector

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude did not provide sufficient guidance on API 653 code compliance. Specifically, when base material data was missing from the initial table, Claude did not ask whether to treat the material as 'unknown' or estimate it based on the tank's construction year, which is essential for accurate wall loss and allowable stress calculations.

Step 1.step_action: Extract nominal thickness, minimum remaining wall thickness (t min), and critical thinning dimensions (L x W) from the provided C-Scan map and thickness histogram.

nodes.label: Narrate the inspection goal while browsing local downloads
nodes.detail: While narrating (in Spanish-accented English) that he wants C-scan images of the Coveñas, Colombia tank shell analyzed, the participant has a Windows file-attach dialog open on his Downloads folder, full of mostly unrelated PDF exports.

nodes.label: Locate and download the C-scan/histogram exports from Google Drive
nodes.detail: Switches to a Chrome tab showing a Google Drive folder named 'Minnesota Nlp' containing the tk701/tk703 C-scan map and histogram PDF exports for tank TK-731, downloading several of them.

nodes.label: Attach the downloaded files to a new Claude chat and request the API 653 report
nodes.detail: Attaches seven files (five P30/histogram scan PDFs plus their histograms and a datasheet image) to a new Claude desktop chat and types: 'this is a scan c on first shell on the tank located in covenas Colombia, attached the dimensions and I would like prepare a report according to API 653,' opening the chat 'API 653 tank inspection report for Coveñas facility.'

nodes.label: Inventory files and flag tank/filename mismatches before drafting
nodes.detail: Lists the uploaded files, rasterizes the unread PDFs, and extracts the text layer from all seven to check for numeric thickness data. Produces a full inventory table and flags three discrepancies before drafting anything: the datasheet is for tank TK-731 (Coveñas) but every scan's embedded title references tk701/tk703 from a folder path pointing to a different terminal (Pozos Colorados); one filename is inconsistent with its own embedded title; and none of the PDFs carry a numeric thickness table, color-scale legend, or CML coordinates. Asks the participant to clarify before proceeding.

nodes.label: Read Claude's file inventory and the flagged tank/filename mismatch
nodes.detail: The participant reads Claude's summary of the seven uploaded files and its warning that the filenames (tk701/tk703) do not match the TK-731 tank in the request, which Claude wants resolved before drafting a formal report.

nodes.label: Waive the filename/tank-ID discrepancy and instruct Claude to proceed
nodes.detail: Replies 'dont matter the name of pdf,' explicitly instructing Claude to proceed with the analysis despite the flagged tank-ID/filename mismatch rather than resolving or re-verifying it.

nodes.label: Assemble, generate, and deliver the draft UT survey report
nodes.detail: Prepares all imagery, writes build_report.js, generates a 10-page docx report, renders it to page images, and spot-checks pages before sharing 'TK731_ShellCourse1_UT_Survey_Report.docx.' Flags that none of the four scan exports include actual numeric thickness values, a color legend, or nominal course thickness -- so only qualitative description of the histogram/map patterns was possible -- and points to Section 7 for what would be needed from the UT contractor to produce a full quantitative report.

nodes.label: Review the draft report page by page
nodes.detail: Reviews the delivered 10-page draft report page by page -- tank ID datasheet fields marked 'N.E.' for not-established, a Limitations-of-Review section noting no numeric thickness legend/calibration reference was included in the exports and that only four grid locations were reviewed, and a Recommendations section calling for the raw numeric CML dataset and nominal thickness table from the UT contractor.

Step 3.step_action: Prompt Claude to apply API 653 Section 4.3.3 formulas for localized shell thinning using the t min and defect length criteria from Step 1.

nodes.label: Ask whether he can calculate the area under corrosion per Section 4.3
nodes.detail: Asks: 'whit the spots at the images, can I calculate the area under corrosion and detrminate the vertical large according to 4.3' -- the technical query that opens this step.

nodes.label: Research the API 653 critical-length methodology and push back on the area-based framing
nodes.detail: Runs three web searches to pin down API 653 Section 4.3.2.1's exact critical-length methodology, then explains that the 'critical length' L is calculated (L = 3.7*sqrt(D x t2) inches, capped at 40in) rather than measured visually off the image, that D (tank diameter, 143.9ft) is already known but t2 is the missing piece since the histograms' thickness axis has no confirmed unit, and that 'area under corrosion' isn't actually an API 653 Section 4.3 input -- the standard uses a 1-D t1/t2/L averaging method, not an area/RSF calculation. Asks the participant to either supply a real t2 reading or confirm the histogram axis is calibrated and in what unit.

nodes.label: Read the draft report while Claude researches the API 653 methodology
nodes.detail: While Claude works on the Section 4.3 question, the participant keeps the draft UT survey report open beside the chat and reads through it, including the limitations and recommendations pages.

nodes.label: Read Claude's explanation that L is calculated, not measured from the C-scan
nodes.detail: The participant reads Claude's reply that the API 653 Section 4.3.2.1 critical length L is calculated from the tank diameter and the lowest reading t2 rather than measured off the C-scan image, and that Claude needs a confirmed t2 value or a calibrated histogram axis (with units) to compute it.

nodes.label: Supply the coupling-dropout assumption for gapped histogram readings
nodes.detail: Instructs Claude: 'the histograms thickness axis is directly calibrated, the points without meausures is because the acoplant was poor, asume that is similar thickness to point around' -- confirming the axis is calibrated and telling Claude how to treat the gapped (poor-couplant) readings, though without yet stating a unit. Also flags that because the shell is riveted construction (API 12B per the datasheet), some 'lower thickness' clusters could be lap-joint/doubler-plate overlap zones rather than corrosion.

nodes.label: Calibrate histogram axes and extract bar-height profiles across all four scans
nodes.detail: Reasons a physical sanity check is needed before trusting the axis units, installs PyMuPDF for vector-level PDF extraction, and inspects the vector drawing objects and embedded raster images in the histogram PDFs. Locates plot frame borders and tick-label positions, confirms axis values read 0.0/10.00/20.00, extracts real physical scan dimensions from the C-scan map PDFs, and auto-calibrates both axes for all four histograms, extracting the full bar-height (percent-of-area) profile for every thickness bin.

nodes.label: Keep the draft report open and reread Claude's earlier Section 4.3.2.1 explanation while it calibrates the histograms
nodes.detail: While Claude calibrates the histogram axes, the participant keeps the draft report open on the right and scrolls back in the chat to reread Claude's earlier explanation of how the critical length works.

nodes.label: Edit and resubmit the instruction to state the axis is in millimeters
nodes.detail: The participant edits the earlier message and resubmits it with the clarification that the histogram thickness axis is calibrated in millimeters, while Claude continues processing.

nodes.label: Debug histogram segmentation, extract peak readings, and deliver L-value calculations
nodes.detail: Re-renders the histograms at higher DPI, iterates through several failed attempts to isolate each plot's true bounding box, and reconciles pixel calibration discrepancies before re-running segmentation with corrected bounds. Delivers the full critical-length calculation assuming mm units: t2/L values for all four locations (Anillo 15-Sector B t2~6mm/L~548mm, Lamina 23B t2~9mm/L~671mm, 10A t2~9mm/L~671mm, 11A-Lateral t2~5mm/L~500mm, all under the 40in cap), flagged as chart-read approximations (+/-1-2mm), and reiterates that 'area under corrosion' is not a Section 4.3 input.

nodes.label: Watch Claude process the histograms, then review the full draft report
nodes.detail: The participant watches Claude run its histogram calibration and segmentation steps without intervening, then expands the draft TK-731 UT survey report to full view and reviews its recommendations section.

nodes.label: Watch Claude continue, then reread its earlier request for t2 and units
nodes.detail: The participant returns to the chat to watch Claude keep debugging the histogram segmentation, then scrolls back to reread Claude's earlier explanation of the area-based framing and its request for a confirmed t2 value and axis units.

nodes.label: Review the L-value results
nodes.detail: The participant reads Claude's critical-length results (L = 3.7*sqrt(D*t2), with t2 read from the histograms assuming millimeters), going through the values for each scan location such as Ring 15 Sector B and Lamina 23B, while the draft report stays open beside the chat.

nodes.label: Ask how much of the shell must be UT-scanned for a defensible criterion
nodes.detail: Asks: 'it was a spot inspection, according to API 653 how many area at the first shell have to be explore by ut corrosion mapping? to determinate a sure criteria.' The question is first sent around 58:30, shortly after a 90% session-limit warning; the recording then pauses for about two hours (the system clock jumps from 11:53 to 14:03), and on returning the participant resends the same question, which is why it appears twice in the chat log.

nodes.label: Research API 653 coverage requirements and explain there is no fixed percentage
nodes.detail: Runs two web searches, then explains API 653 sets no fixed area/percentage requirement for whole-course UT coverage -- the only explicit minimum (Section 4.3.2.1(c), 5 equally spaced readings) applies only after a suspect area is already found -- and sizes up the participant's actual coverage: the four scans total roughly 2-3% of Course 1's surface, with 2 of the 4 spots already showing secondary thinning as a trigger to expand rather than stop. Closes with the bottom line that documented rationale, not a code percentage, is what makes a spot-check defensible.

nodes.label: Review the coverage assessment
nodes.detail: Reviews the coverage explanation, weighing the ~2-3% sample against the two spots already showing secondary thinning.

Step 2.step_name: Operational Fluid & Internal Corrosion Mechanism Profiling
Step 2.step_action: Consult Claude to analyze internal corrosion mechanisms typical for crude oil storage (BS&W settling, localized pitting, sludge) in tropical coastal conditions in Colombia.

nodes.label: Open the site-specification reference and request the weather/climate update
nodes.detail: Opens a second reference document on Google Drive, 'ANEXO 4 ESPECIFICACIONES TECNICAS,' a Spanish-language technical specification for the Coveñas CENIT terminal showing the tank's location, site infrastructure map, and stated average climate of 38 degrees C, then asks Claude, in the same ongoing chat, to factor the weather conditions at Coveñas, Colombia, including future climate-change trends, and the type of liquid stored, into the report -- and to update the final report with a full inspection plan.

nodes.label: Research corrosion mechanisms, finalize and review the updated report
nodes.detail: Researches Coveñas/Sucre climate, Caribbean tropical-storm risks under climate change, and Ecopetrol's Coveñas terminal and crude storage operations. Develops a corrosion-mechanism discussion linking sea-level rise, site elevation, and increasing cyclone intensity to crude-specific internal and external corrosion risks, including bottom-water MIC, riveted lap-joint crevice corrosion, vapor-space condensation, and atmospheric attack. Confirms earlier reference assets remain available, completes the updated report, reviews Claude's summary, and checks the downloaded document. The session ends with this self-review; no on-screen completion of the Output Quality or Collaboration Assessment fields is observed.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about researching Coveñas climate and crude-specific corrosion mechanisms
nodes.detail: The participant reads Claude's summary of the updated 16-page report, which adds an executive summary, Coveñas climate and crude-specific corrosion mechanisms, and an inspection plan section.

Step 4.step_action: Review Claude's generated calculations and compliance text against client specifications and NDT C-Scan raw data, assembling the final inspection report.

nodes.label: Review and confirm the finished report, then close out the session
nodes.detail: Reviews Claude's summary of the new report content and checks the downloaded document. The recording ends with this self-review of the finished report still the last visible activity; no on-screen filling of the workflow document's Output Quality and Collaboration Assessment fields is observed.

Step 1.step_action: Extract nominal thickness, minimum remaining wall thickness (t min), and critical thinning dimensions (L x W) from the provided C-Scan map and thickness histogram.
Step 1.input: C-Scan  file and thickness histogram graphic.
Step 1.output: Summary table of measured minimum thickness and spatial bounds of wall loss.
rubrics: Accurate identification of nominal vs. minimum remaining wall thickness
Precise measurement of the critical defect boundaries (L x W).

ratings.output_quality_reason: The output was too generic. I expected Claude to analyze historical manufacturing context—for example, prompting me on whether steels produced during that tank's construction era typically exhibit center-line defects or laminations due to the steelmaking process of that time.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Even though the initial input was clear, the agent failed to identify missing material properties and did not prompt for manufacturing context.

Step 2.step_name: Operational Fluid & Internal Corrosion Mechanism Profiling
Step 2.step_action: Consult Claude to analyze internal corrosion mechanisms typical for crude oil storage (BS&W settling, localized pitting, sludge) in tropical coastal conditions in Colombia.
Step 2.input: Operating temperature (~38°C), crude fluid parameters, marine environment context.
Step 2.output: Risk assessment profile detailing expected internal corrosion drivers and metal loss rates.
rubrics: Technical accuracy regarding crude oil BS&W bottom settling corrosion
Alignment between environmental temperature/salinity and expected corrosion rates

ratings.output_quality_reason: The output interpreted the signals as corrosion, but it failed to consider manufacturing/steelmaking defects (e.g., center-line segregation or inclusions) typical of the material's vintage.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: It failed to recognize coverage limitations. If the input represents only a partial scan, the agent should have suggested expanding the scan area—especially when a heavily corroded region is concentrated near the center of the inspected grid.

Step 3.step_action: Prompt Claude to apply API 653 Section 4.3.3 formulas for localized shell thinning using the t min and defect length criteria from Step 1.
Step 3.input: C-scan histogram distribution data and API 653 evaluation equations.
Step 3.output: Structural integrity evaluation statement and API 653 compliance summary.
rubrics: Correct application of API 653 Section 4.3.3 acceptance limits t min )
Clear engineering conclusion (Pass/Fail or repair recommendation)

ratings.output_quality_reason: Claude correctly applied the API 653 Section 4.3.3 evaluation formulas for localized shell thinning using the minimum thickness (t min) and critical defect length (L).

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The agent correctly applied the required API 653 Section 4.3.3 formulas.

Step 4.step_action: Review Claude's generated calculations and compliance text against client specifications and NDT C-Scan raw data, assembling the final inspection report.
Step 4.output: Completed API 653 Fitness-for-Service evaluation report ready for client submission.
rubrics: Complete alignment between AI-generated evaluations and raw NDT scan data
Professional engineering report structure with clear actionable recommendations

ratings.output_quality_reason: The overall structure of the final report was well-organized, and the conclusions aligned properly with API 653 requirements despite the limited input data. However, I would have preferred Claude to explicitly cite the specific API 653 clauses/sections applied and explain their technical importance within the report.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: It generate a report with structure
